# CPU1 (Cortex-M33) first-party warning-profile escape inventory -- issue #843.
#
# Each row is a FIRST-PARTY translation unit on a CPU1 executable that
# ra8_add_cpu1_image()'s per-source profile (-Wall -Wextra -Werror ...
# -Wstack-usage=2048 -fstack-usage) never reaches: it compiles at
# -mcpu=cortex-m33 ... -Os with no warning flags and emits no .su stack data.
# These are the sources #843 must bring onto the bar. Two ways a TU lands here:
#
#   * the app bolts it onto a helper-built image with its own target_sources(),
#     and the helper scopes the profile to its own SOURCES (compile_on_m33,
#     ereader_m33);
#   * the app HAND-ROLLS the CPU1 executable with add_executable() plus its own
#     -mcpu=cortex-m33 options and never calls the helper, so NOTHING on that
#     image carries the profile, its own cpu1_main.c included (cpu1_pingpong,
#     cpu1_pingpong_ipc).
#
# Format: <cpu1-target>  <repo-relative source path>
#
# scripts/checks/check_cpu1_warning_profile.py judges this file. The list is
# SHRINK-ONLY: a first-party CPU1 .c source that is not here fails the gate, and
# a row that stops escaping (profile-covered, detached from the image, or
# deleted) fails as stale and must be removed. Never add a row to silence a new
# escape without saying why in review. Vendored SOUP never belongs here: it is
# deliberately outside the first-party bar and the gate rejects such a row.
#
# WHAT THIS INVENTORY DOES NOT COVER -- said plainly rather than implied by the
# rule above. The checker resolves a source token only when it ends in ".c":
# resolve_source() returns the empty list for every other suffix, and
# glob_vars() skips a file(GLOB ...) pattern that does not end in ".c", ".h" or
# "*". So a first-party .cpp / .cc / .S / .s translation unit bolted onto a CPU1
# image is neither profile-covered nor an escape row: it is dropped with no
# finding and the gate still prints a clean run. Every row below is .c because
# .c is all the parser can see, so this gate's own output can never tell you
# whether the tree holds such a TU today.
#
# A hand census can, and one was taken on 2026-09-17: the tree has ten CPU1
# images, every source token on every one of them is .c, and the uncovered
# shape is therefore LATENT rather than live.
#
#   * Eight images are helper-built and pass only SOURCES src/cpu1_main.c,
#     which the per-source profile does reach: blink_m33, blink_m33_hal,
#     cache_coherency_hil, compile_on_m33, dualcore_background_m33,
#     dualcore_mailbox, ereader_m33, lowpower_holdpage.
#   * Exactly two of those bolt more on with target_sources(): compile_on_m33
#     (21 first-party .c, counting the epub/src/*.c glob, plus vendored
#     miniz.c, which is SOUP and correctly not a row) and ereader_m33 (4 .c).
#     Established by reading both listfiles and by a repo-wide search for
#     target_sources() on a *_cpu1.elf target, which returns those two alone.
#   * The two hand-rolled images name four .c sources each in add_executable()
#     (cpu1_pingpong, cpu1_pingpong_ipc), read in full.
#
# 21 + 4 + 4 + 4 is exactly the 33 rows below, so this inventory is currently
# complete for the .c set as well as scoped to it. The census is a human read
# of the listfiles rather than a gate run, so it decays the moment one of them
# changes: that is the argument for teaching the parser the other suffixes
# instead of trusting this paragraph. The repo does compile first-party C++
# elsewhere (apps/shared_libs/reflow/v2/src/reflow_v2.cpp), so the shape stays
# live. Read the SHRINK-ONLY rule as scoped to .c until the parser measures
# the rest.
#
# A missing or unreadable file yields the EMPTY set, so every escape reports.
# The gate fails closed.
#
# The "#! rows:" line below declares how many rows this file holds and the gate
# fails when it disagrees with the rows it parses. That is what lets this file
# legitimately reach zero rows when #843 is paid off: an intact inventory can
# declare "#! rows: 0", while a truncated or hand-emptied one carries no
# matching declaration and still fails closed.
#! rows: 8
cpu1_pingpong_cpu1.elf  examples/ek_ra8d2/hw_validated/hil/cpu1_pingpong/src/cpu1_main.c
cpu1_pingpong_cpu1.elf  libs/ra8_core/src/ra8_log.c
cpu1_pingpong_cpu1.elf  libs/ra8_core/src/ra8_scb.c
cpu1_pingpong_cpu1.elf  libs/ra8_hal/src/ra8_ipc.c
cpu1_pingpong_ipc_cpu1.elf  examples/ek_ra8d2/hil_needs_revalidation/cpu1_pingpong_ipc/src/cpu1_main.c
cpu1_pingpong_ipc_cpu1.elf  libs/ra8_core/src/ra8_log.c
cpu1_pingpong_ipc_cpu1.elf  libs/ra8_core/src/ra8_scb.c
cpu1_pingpong_ipc_cpu1.elf  libs/ra8_hal/src/ra8_ipc.c
